textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 science · Life Processes in Plants · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Photosynthesis is how green plants make food. Leaves take in carbon dioxide from air through tiny pores called stomata, and roots take in water.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Photosynthesis is how green plants make food. Leaves take in carbon dioxide from air through tiny pores called stomata, and roots take in water. Chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves, captures sunlight.
beats.speakEn: Photosynthesis is how green plants make food. Leaves take in carbon dioxide from air through tiny pores called stomata, and roots take in water. Chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves, captures sunlight.

beats.en: Roots take water and minerals from the soil. Xylem tubes carry water upward to the leaves. Phloem tubes carry food from leaves to other parts.
beats.speakEn: Roots take water and minerals from the soil. Xylem tubes carry water upward to the leaves. Phloem tubes carry food from leaves to other parts.

type: Key Concept: Photosynthesis is how green plants make food.
Rule: Roots take water and minerals from the soil. Xylem tubes carry water upward to the leaves.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 science · Life Processes in Plants · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Transpiration is the loss of water as vapour from the leaves through stomata. It cools the plant and pulls water up from the roots.

beats.en: Transpiration is the loss of water as vapour from the leaves through stomata. It cools the plant and pulls water up from the roots.
beats.speakEn: Transpiration is the loss of water as vapour from the leaves through stomata. It cools the plant and pulls water up from the roots.

beats.en: Plants also respire: they take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide, day and night. Some plants, like insect-eating pitcher plants, get extra nutrients from insects.
beats.speakEn: Plants also respire: they take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide, day and night. Some plants, like insect-eating pitcher plants, get extra nutrients from insects.

type: Transpiration is the loss of water as vapour from the leaves through stomata.
Plants also respire: they take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide, day and night.
